title: First-line TB drugs
dek: HRZE is still the mental model: cidal INH, sterilizing rifamycin, pH-active PZA, companion EMB. The 4-month rifapentine–moxifloxacin regimen is the 2022 update, not a replacement for knowing HRZE.
story: Isoniazid is a prodrug. KatG (catalase-peroxidase) activates it; the INH–NAD adduct inhibits InhA and collapses FAS-II mycolate synthesis. It is rapidly cidal against replicating bacilli. katG S315T is the common high-level resistance allele; inhA promoter up-regulation gives lower-level INH resistance and ethionamide cross-resistance.

Rifampin is the sterilizing rifamycin of the classical backbone (see the rifampin plate). Pyrazinamide is also a prodrug: PncA (pyrazinamidase) yields pyrazinoic acid. Activity is strongly pH-dependent and especially useful in acidic, inflammatory, necrotic lesions. Ethambutol inhibits arabinosyltransferases (EmbCAB, clinically EmbB) and is the companion that protects against resistance while susceptibility is still being proven.

Standard DS-TB was 2HRZE/4HR. WHO now also recommends a 4-month regimen of isoniazid, rifapentine, moxifloxacin, and pyrazinamide (HPMZ) for eligible patients. Knowing both is part of not being stuck in 2010.
deep: INH and PZA both require bacterial enzymes. Loss-of-function is an easy resistance route: missense in katG, and a long tail of pncA coding and promoter mutations scattered across the gene (no tidy RRDR). That is why pncA needs whole-gene interrogation, not a five-probe cartridge.
EmbB Met306 variants are the common ethambutol story, but ethambutol DST has always been fiddly; WGS catalogues are more honest if you report confidence grades.

Rifapentine is a longer-half-life rifamycin used in LTBI (3HP) and in the 4-month HPMZ DS-TB regimen. CYP3A4 induction still happens. Moxifloxacin in HPMZ is a first-line drug in that regimen and a second-line drug in RR-TB — the same molecule, different neighbors.
HIV, pregnancy, and extensive disease still force regimen thinking beyond a mnemonic. PZA is often used in TB meningitis; EMB’s optic neuropathy is the monitoring tax.

example.title: Low-level INH resistance and ethionamide
example.setup: WGS: inhA c-15t promoter mutation, katG wild type. Phenotypic INH MIC is 0.25 µg/mL (above the 0.1 critical concentration, below high-level). The team wants to know about ethionamide.

steps.title: What c-15t does
steps.body: Promoter up-regulation makes more InhA. INH (and ethionamide, which also ends at InhA) need higher concentrations. This is not KatG failure; some INH activity may remain at higher dose in selected regimens, depending on current guidance.

steps.title: Cross-resistance
steps.body: Ethionamide/prothionamide share the InhA endpoint. An inhA promoter mutant is a poor candidate for ETH even if katG is intact.
steps.expression: inhA promoter ↑  →  INH low-level R  +  ETH cross-R

steps.title: What you still do not know
steps.body: This result does not speak to rifampin, PZA, or FQ. Do not collapse the entire DST into the INH story.

example.takeaway: katG vs inhA is a quantitative and a cross-resistance distinction, not two ways to write “INH-R.”

check.prompt: Which pair are prodrugs that require Mtb enzymes for activation?
check.why: KatG activates INH; PncA activates PZA. RIF and EMB bind their targets without that activation step.

check.prompt: katG S315T typically produces which INH phenotype, compared with an inhA promoter mutant?
choices: Lower-level INH resistance with ETH cross-resistance
High-level INH resistance, usually without obligatory ETH cross-resistance
No INH effect; only streptomycin resistance
check.answer: High-level INH resistance, usually without obligatory ETH cross-resistance
check.why: S315T degrades activation of INH while leaving InhA itself intact, so ETH (which uses EthA, then InhA) is often spared. Promoter inhA mutants are the ETH-cross story.

whyWrong.Lower-level INH resistance with ETH cros: That is the inhA promoter pattern.

check.prompt: On the mechanism map, what sits between PZA and “POA / CoA stress”?
check.figureHint: Follow the bottom row of nodes.
check.why: Pyrazinamidase converts PZA to pyrazinoic acid. KatG is the INH row; RpoB is RIF; EmbCAB is EMB.

whyWrong.KatG: That is the INH activation node.
